stem: When an electrolyte solution is diluted,
model_answer: **(b).** Fewer ions per unit volume, so $\kappa$ falls; ions from one mole are freer (or more of them, for weak electrolytes), so $\Lambda_m$ rises.

stem: Define molar conductivity. With a sketch, show how it varies with $\sqrt c$ for a strong and a weak electrolyte.
model_answer:
**Molar conductivity** is the conductivity of a solution divided by its molar concentration, $\Lambda_m=\kappa/c$ (S cm$^2$mol$^{-1}$): the conducting power of all ions from one mole of electrolyte. [½]
*(graph to be added as SVG)* Strong: small, linear rise on dilution, $\Lambda_m=\Lambda_m^\circ-A\sqrt c$ (ions move more freely). Weak: steep rise at low concentration because the degree of dissociation increases. [1 + ½ graph]

stem: Write the anode, cathode and overall reactions of the lead storage battery during discharge. What happens to the density of the electrolyte?
model_answer:
Anode: $\ce{Pb(s) + SO4^2-(aq) -> PbSO4(s) + 2e-}$ [½]
Cathode: $\ce{PbO2(s) + SO4^2-(aq) + 4H+(aq) + 2e- -> PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l)}$ [½]
Overall: $\ce{Pb + PbO2 + 2H2SO4 -> 2PbSO4 + 2H2O}$ [½]
Density **decreases**: H$_2$SO$_4$ is used up and water is formed. [½]

scheme.step: Density **decreases**: H$_2$SO$_4$ is used up and water is formed.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
Calculate the emf at 298 K of the cell
$\ce{Sn(s) | Sn^2+(0.004 M) || H+(0.020 M) | H2(g, 1 bar) | Pt(s)}$
Given $E^\circ_{\ce{Sn^2+/Sn}}=-0.14$ V.
model_answer:
Cell reaction: $\ce{Sn(s) + 2H+(aq) -> Sn^2+(aq) + H2(g)}$, $n=2$ [½]
$E^\circ_\text{cell}=E^\circ_\text{cathode}-E^\circ_\text{anode}=0.00-(-0.14)=0.14$ V [½]
$E_\text{cell}=E^\circ_\text{cell}-\dfrac{0.059}{2}\log\dfrac{[\ce{Sn^2+}]\,p_{\ce{H2}}}{[\ce{H+}]^2}$ [1]
$=0.14-0.0295\log\dfrac{0.004}{(0.020)^2}=0.14-0.0295\log10=\boxed{0.11\text{ V}}$ [1]

label: PYQ-style
stem: A conductivity cell filled with 0.1 M KCl has resistance 100 $\Omega$. Filled with 0.02 M KCl it has resistance 520 $\Omega$. The conductivity of 0.1 M KCl is 1.29 S m$^{-1}$. Calculate the conductivity and molar conductivity of 0.02 M KCl.
model_answer:
Cell constant $G^*=\kappa R=1.29$ S m$^{-1}\times100\ \Omega=129$ m$^{-1}$ [1]
$\kappa_{0.02\text{ M}}=\dfrac{G^*}{R}=\dfrac{129}{520}=0.248$ S m$^{-1}$ $=\boxed{2.48\times10^{-3}\text{ S cm}^{-1}}$ [1]
$\Lambda_m=\dfrac{1000\,\kappa}{M}=\dfrac{1000\times2.48\times10^{-3}}{0.02}=\boxed{124\text{ S cm}^2\text{mol}^{-1}}$ [1]

scheme.step: Cell constant $G^*=\kappa R=1.29$ S m$^{-1}\times100\ \Omega=129$ m$^{-1}$

label: PYQ-style
stem: (a) State Kohlrausch's law. (b) $\Lambda^\circ_m$ for NaCl, HCl and CH$_3$COONa are 126.4, 425.9 and 91.0 S cm$^2$mol$^{-1}$. Find $\Lambda^\circ_m$ of CH$_3$COOH. (c) Why can't this value be found by extrapolating a graph?
model_answer:
(a) **Kohlrausch's law:** the limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte is the sum of the individual contributions of its cation and anion, $\Lambda_m^\circ=\nu_+\lambda_+^\circ+\nu_-\lambda_-^\circ$. [1]
(b) $\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{CH3COOH}}=\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{CH3COONa}}+\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{HCl}}-\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{NaCl}}=91.0+425.9-126.4=\boxed{390.5\text{ S cm}^2\text{mol}^{-1}}$ [1]
(c) For a weak electrolyte $\Lambda_m$ rises very steeply at low concentration (dissociation keeps increasing), so the curve cannot be extended to zero concentration. [1]

label: PYQ-style
stem:
(a) For $\ce{2Fe^3+(aq) + 2I-(aq) -> 2Fe^2+(aq) + I2(s)}$, $E^\circ_\text{cell}=0.236$ V at 298 K. Calculate $\Delta_rG^\circ$ and the equilibrium constant. (F = 96500 C mol$^{-1}$) [3]
(b) How many faradays are needed to deposit 1 mol of Al from molten $\ce{Al2O3}$? [1]
(c) Write the electrode reactions of the H$_2$–O$_2$ fuel cell. [1]
model_answer:
(a) $n=2$. $\Delta_rG^\circ=-nFE^\circ_\text{cell}$ [½] $=-2\times96500\times0.236=-45548$ J mol$^{-1}$ $=\boxed{-45.55\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}}$ [1]
$\log K_c=\dfrac{nE^\circ_\text{cell}}{0.059}$ [½] $=\dfrac{2\times0.236}{0.059}=8.0$ ⇒ $K_c=\boxed{1\times10^{8}}$ [1]
(b) $\ce{Al^3+ + 3e- -> Al}$: **3 F** per mole of Al. [1]
(c) Cathode: $\ce{O2(g) + 2H2O(l) + 4e- -> 4OH-(aq)}$ [½]
Anode: $\ce{2H2(g) + 4OH-(aq) -> 4H2O(l) + 4e-}$ [½]

scheme.step: (b) $\ce{Al^3+ + 3e- -> Al}$: **3 F** per mole of Al.
